text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index finished at a record peak for the eight consecutive session on Tuesday, despite a wave of profit-taking on Wall Street. The leading blue chip index, up for the eleventh straight session, added 21.4 points to close at 4,691.0, as advancers beat decliners by a margin of two to one.

FRANKFURT - German share advance regains momentum to end bourse trade at a record DAX closing level. Activity still focused on individual shares, but many dealers say overall sentiment bullish, broad market targeting further record highs. Gains sparked by Wall Street advance. The DAX index closed up 19.78 points at 3,595.15. In post-bourse trade the index stood at 3,559.29 down 33.85.

PARIS - French shares closed with a big gain on Tuesday but remained below an all-time high. Shares were boosted by a strong gain on Wall Street on Monday night and on new opinion polls showing a lead for the ruling centre-right majority. The CAC-40 index closed up 26.49 points or 0.98 percent at 2,719.58. ZURICH - Swiss shares ended narrowly off the intra-day high, but were still able to post a second closing high. Foreign buying, a recovery in the U.S. dollar and Wall Street's overnight gains were the main reasons behind the rise, dealers said. Also, several shares were in demand due to warrant issues. The All share SPI index closed up 25.39 points at 3,212.87.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed mixed on Tuesday. Steadiness in the yen/dollar rate initially stimulated buying in major high-tech shares such as Sony Corp, but the buying momentum ran out of steam later. The 225-share Nikkei average ended 14.40 points lower or 0.07 percent at 20,129.11.

HONG KONG - After nine consecutive winning sessions, Hong Kong share prices finally gave up some ground on Tuesday, ending weaker as stocks ran into profit-taking and the Hang Seng Index met resistance above 14,000 points. The index fell 81.34 points, or 0.58 percent, to close at 13,906.46.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market set closing and intraday record highs on Tuesday, taking its cue from another record run on Wall Street. The All Ordinaries index added 9.5 points to close at 2,534.3.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares edge slightly firmer at close of mixed Tuesday's trade after retracing early losses. Dealers say golds cheered by late rises in the bullion price, spurred by some dollar weakness. Bullion last bid at $348.20 an ounce. Golds last up 7.6 points to 1,275.4, industrials down 1.4 points to 8,474.7 and all-share up 2.8 points to 7,193.1.
